HelpingHand

Putting Robotics Within Every Student's Grasp

We make robotics more affordable and easier to learn, so students ages 11 and up can move from following a guide to designing, building, and testing their own inventions.

Build one finger.

Start with a guide. Assemble the links, connect the motor, and watch the joints curl together.

See what moves.

Follow the motion from the drive to the fingertip. Each link gives you a place to ask what would happen if you changed it.

Try your own design.

Change a link, predict how the grip will move, then test it. Your next design starts with what you learn.

The kit

Engineered for hands-on learning.

HelpingHand is a modular robotic hand that students CAD, wire, and program themselves. They learn mechanics, circuits, and coding concepts one lesson at a time, without following a finished kit.

See the kit

Mechanics

Small links. Coordinated movement.

Each finger is a linkage. Explore how connected links carry one motor's motion to the fingertip.

Electronics

A little power. A lot to explore.

An Arduino Mega runs six DC motors, with two push buttons to drive them.

Programming

From your code to its fingertips.

Program the grasp, run it from the buttons, then change the sketch and watch the hand respond.
